title: Accountability
definition: Accountability is the loving practice of helping one another walk faithfully through honesty, encouragement, correction, prayer, and responsibility.
summary: Accountability helps believers resist sin and grow in faithful obedience.
christFocus: Jesus shepherds His people through truth and grace, and He uses the body of Christ to help believers endure.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Accountability is not control, shame, or spiritual policing. It is loving help within the body of Christ. Believers need others who will pray, encourage, ask honest questions, and speak truth in love.

Accountability is especially important where sin thrives in secrecy. Confession, prayer, and wise support help believers resist temptation and pursue restoration.

Healthy accountability points to Christ, not dependence on a person. It should be marked by humility, confidentiality, truth, grace, and practical follow-through.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people remain trapped because they battle sin, addiction, shame, or discouragement alone. Accountability matters because God designed believers to help carry one another's burdens.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Invite a mature believer into areas where you need prayer and honesty. Be truthful, receive correction humbly, and offer accountability to others with gentleness rather than superiority.
